account:
Today I have followed my appointments: morning correspondence, a ten o'clock market walk, noon at home, and now the one o'clock town accounts appointment with the secretary. I have just asked for the accounts and any business requiring my decision, but have not yet received a report. Tea is arranged for three at the neighbour's cottage, road point (16, -60, 105), beside the east-bank ferry; I am due back in the office at 16:30 and home at 19:00.

The most noticeable news has been several townsfolk repeating that the baker was carrying a sack of bread at the inn. Townsfolk 10, 20, 30, 18 and 08 were among those I heard passing this along. I did not see the delivery myself. It could simply be bread supplied to the inn; I have no evidence of anything improper or a special purpose. The repetition is more striking than the reported event itself.

The builder was looking for the innkeeper or freight operator about supplies. I asked what was needed, but have not learned the details, so I cannot say whether this is routine purchasing or a difficulty needing town assistance. I do not know of a connection between that inquiry and the baker's bread.

The secretary has been helping with appointments and asked the neighbour to confirm the tea location. I bought two fresh loaves at the market, intending them for lunch and tea. Otherwise, I have not directly observed any unusual disruption in town.
